purpose: Implement story-scoped changes on dedicated branches using the approved contract, tests, and knowledge base context.
validation: decision and assumption changes are recorded
no unauthorized tool or resource use
A fresh project no longer reports six irrelevant bootstrap decisions.
Requirement intake is not contract-gated and decomposition requires an approved requirement before a contract.
Root help and starter prompts lead naturally to assessment, new PR, existing PR, or local-only work.
All runtime-required inputs are present in command help and all blocked steps expose an actionable next step.
Targeted tests, full npm test, npm run check, npm run doctor, package verification, independent novice replay, strict gate, and remote CI pass.

contextualization.summary: Correct the public first-time-user journey without adding natural-language classification to the deterministic CLI: Codex translates the user's request; the CLI validates and persists the agreed sequence.

context_sources.excerpt: acceptance_criteria Effective configuration is versioned hash-locked explainable and migrated only through a reviewed plan hash; plugin upgrades cannot silently activate authority autonomy gate or budget defaults. A versioned workflow-definition and event-sourced workflow-instance engine supports software-project change-request technical-assessment and generic-governed-process presets without replacing the existing six SDLC execution phases. Requirement ceilings and a separate non-reusable delivery profile preserve an explicit autonomy choice for every pull request or local release with fail-closed action receipts and compatibility for existing v1 records. Deterministic enterprise fixtures exercise at least 1 000 stories 10 000 records 5 000 dependency edges and 100 000 trace events; orchestration and query remain within 2 seconds on Unix and 4 seconds on Windows warm Observatory reads remain within 100 milliseconds on Unix and 250 milliseconds on Windows and RSS remains within 256 MiB on Unix and 320 MiB on Windows. questions.question: What is the user-facing sequence?
questions.answer: Describe outcome and delivery target; agree outcome, acceptance criteria and non-goals; decompose only when needed; agree output and work brief; choose autonomy once for this PR; start once; implement, verify, push and merge within the displayed boundary.

questions.question: Which delivery is in scope?
questions.answer: One pull request from codex/ST-NOVICE-PLUGIN-JOURNEY to main in github.com/aantenore/agentic-sdlc-codex-plugin.

questions.question: What must a novice never need for normal use?
questions.answer: Internal IDs, canonical JSON, hashes, receipt vocabulary, or CLI recovery flags; these remain optional technical details.

questions.question: What actions are excluded?
questions.answer: Installs, secrets, production, external services, remote deployment, destructive work, and scope expansion.

constraints: Preserve deterministic structured CLI behavior, Node 18.18+ compatibility, stable JSON fields, assessment two-checkpoint behavior, and existing safety gates.
Untouched bootstrap phase contracts remain available internally but must not appear as current user decisions until activated by a phase or story.
Every blocked public step provides one concrete conversational answer or complete executable recovery action without scope drift.

approvals.summary: Approve the refreshed novice-journey work brief for the same exact PR: deterministic CLI remains structured; Codex provides the natural-language front door; bootstrap noise, lifecycle order, help, starters, documentation, and regression coverage are corrected without expanding tools or access.

scope.principle: An automation approval is valid only under an explicit delegated approval level or configured automation policy recorded in the summary or evidence.
scope.approval_level: Refresh only the outdated internal project snapshot and its content-bound records, then complete ST-NOVICE-PLUGIN-JOURNEY in the already selected pull request from codex/ST-NOVICE-PLUGIN-JOURNEY to main; no requirement, delivery target, write boundary, tool, install, secret, production, external service, deployment, destructive action, or scope expansion.
